worldattribute-terraindiffusionEnabled-d: Generate terrain and climate with the Terrain Diffusion neural model instead of the vanilla landform generator.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionScale-des: How many real-world metres one block represents, horizontally and vertically alike.
worldconfig-terraindiffusionScale-30: 30 m per block (most terrain per step)
worldattribute-terraindiffusionVerticalE: Multiplies terrain height above sea level. At 1x a block is exactly as tall as it is wide.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionClimate-d: Whether the model drives the climate as well as the terrain. The model predicts real bioclimatic variables which set the world's temperature, rainfall, forests and seasons.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionCoarsePoo: Packs more landscape into the same distance: the model's large-scale map is drawn as usual and every 2x2 or 4x4 block of it squeezed into one cell, so continents, ranges and valleys come closer together and the relief between them steepens. It stays realistic because the model is never asked for anything it was not trained on; 4x is dramatic.

How each squeezed block becomes one cell. Average keeps it realistic. Extreme keeps the highest ground and the deepest valley floor of each block, for taller peaks and deeper cuts, at some cost to realism. Does nothing with terrain intensity off.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionInference: Which execution provider runs the model. OpenVINO is primarily for Linux servers. TensorRT RTX needs a GeForce RTX 30xx or newer on Windows or Linux and is roughly 1.5x faster than CUDA. CUDA is another option for Nvidia GPUs. "auto" picks CoreML on macOS, DirectML on Windows, CUDA on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU and the CUDA toolkit installed, and the CPU everywhere else. Changing provider can alter newly generated terrain slightly. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionDecoderPr: FP32 is the default. FP16 provides better performance, but kinda sucks atm. INT8 is a smaller decoder for the CPU and OpenVINO. Neither is ever selected automatically because both can alter newly generated terrain slightly. FP16 needs a GPU provider, a world set to it on a machine without one does not load.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionBasePreci: The base model is most of the work in a tile. FP16 with TensorRT-RTX is the fastest, but the default is FP32 until the FP16 model can be improved. FP16 needs a GPU provider, a world set to it on a machine without one does not load.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionCoarsePre: The coarse model is a small and fast, even at FP32. Use FP32 unless you have measured otherwise. FP16 needs a GPU provider, a world set to it on a machine without one does not load.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionGpuUtiliz: Share of the time world generation may keep the inference device busy. Tweaking this may help with stuttering, but can also cause stuttering. Can be changed with /tdiff gpulimit in game.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionOffloadMo: Keep only one of the three models on the GPU at a time. Holds peak VRAM near 1.5 GB instead of about 2.5 GB, and roughly triples the time per terrain tile. Turn on only if the models will not fit on the card. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionModelLoad: Open model graphs directly from their files, or read them into memory first, which costs roughly 1 GB of temporary RAM. Only use from memory if you are also forced to offload models.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionValidateM: Check the SHA-256 of model files already on disk at every start. Turning this off saves a few seconds per start; file sizes are still checked. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionDownloadR: Fetch the matching ONNX Runtime and, when selected, OpenVINO native libraries automatically. Turn off to supply them yourself in TerrainDiffusionModels/onnxruntime/. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
